closing.reason: (1) Entry points: adopt_partition has one, and nothing in pgpm_core/pgpm_archive/pgpm_hypertable calls it. The new inline refusal fires before the null check and every lock. Under READ COMMITTED a volatile plpgsql function takes a fresh snapshot per statement, so every read the body makes after the lock is current. The refusal itself holds. (2) Resume, upgrade and scheduled paths do not apply: it is a function, replaced by CREATE OR REPLACE, with no tick caller. (3) The body says 'every judgement after that lock ... is only worth the lock when its snapshot was taken after the lock was granted' and the header promises 'the relation judged attached is still attached when its row commits'. That promise breaks in READ COMMITTED because the lock is taken BY NAME: execute format('lock table %s ...', p_child::text). When another session renames the partition and creates a standalone table under the old name, committing while the call waits on that name, LOCK TABLE re-resolves the name after the wait and locks the new table. The oid re-read then passes (a fresh snapshot, the partition still attached), and the row is recorded with no lock on the relation it records. A DETACH then commits before the caller's transaction does, so pgpm.part records a standalone table as a partition, which is #1262's consequence. V-01 shows this on the head and the base alike (pg_locks: 0 locks on the recorded oid; pg_inherits: not a partition at commit). It is pre_existing, Tier 3, and inside the PR's surface (the function and the lock its argument relies on), with a different mechanism (name versus oid), so it does not block landing as a T1/T2 would. (4) The guard asserts the contract (refused, nothing recorded, LIVENESS witnesses). The single mutation (if false) restores this defect exactly: ACC-01 and ACC-02 fail on the mutant. (5) Contract change: an RR/SERIALIZABLE caller is now refused with a named remedy. That workflow was never documented as supported, and the change is in reference.md and CHANGELOG. EXTRA TASK: the acceptance reproductions' head failures come from the fix changing what the reproduction observes, not from a failure to fix. ACC-01 pinned the membership message, and the head refuses earlier with the isolation message while assertion 5 (nothing recorded) passes. ACC-02 called adopt_partition bare in REPEATABLE READ, so the refusal aborted psql before the contract assertion ran. Both were rebuilt as repro.verified.sql, pinning pgpm's refusal ('pg_partition_magician: %') plus nothing recorded, with LIVENESS kept. Results: ACC-01 base FAIL (3,5), head PASS 5/5, mutant FAIL (3,5); ACC-02 base FAIL (3,5), head PASS 7/7, mutant FAIL (3,5).
